articles.body:
I have one question.
If in a region the crown is president und commander as well can i force the commander (with my cubes) to buy local alliances? The crown book says, that i can do that only if i am the president? is that correct?
articles.bodyXml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>I have one question.<br/>If in a region the crown is president und commander as well can i force the commander (with my cubes) to buy local alliances? The crown book says, that i can do that only if i am the president? is that correct?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body:
That is not correct, no.

If the Crown is Commander and either WANTS to buy a Local Alliance, or is bribed (by you) to buy a Local Alliance, then a Crown President will ALWAYS give consent; Crown Handbook, page 11, "If the Crown is Commander:"

[q]Crown Presidents will always give consent to purchasing Local Alliances to Crown Commanders.[/q]

And you can bribe a Crown Commander to buy local alliances, depending on their mood: for example, a Bull, Stag or Lion Commander will be persuaded to buy a local alliance for 2 promise cubes.

[imageid=7729004 medium]

articles.body:
Thanks for that fast answer.
But i have an additional question:
For example: the climate ist bullish, the crown has a commander and the crown has also the presidency, then the crown "will not purchase a local alliance" (Rulebook Crown). Then i can not bribe the crown, because i have not the presidency?
According the rulebook i can only bribe the crown if i have the presidency and the crown is commander: "Will purchase an additional local alliance, ...., if they purchase in YOUR presidency"

Or can i always decide, that the crown should buy an alliance, if the crown is commander AND president?

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>Thanks for that fast answer.<br/>But i have an additional question:<br/>For example: the climate ist bullish, the crown has a commander and the crown has also the presidency, then the crown "will not purchase a local alliance" (Rulebook Crown). Then i can not bribe the crown, because i have not the presidency?<br/>According the rulebook i can only bribe the crown if i have the presidency and the crown is commander: "Will purchase an additional local alliance, ...., if they purchase in YOUR presidency"<br/><br/>Or can i always decide, that the crown should buy an alliance, if the crown is commander AND president?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body:
It does not say you only bribe the crown if you have the presidency; rather, it says you MUST give consent to the Crown if you are the president: I.e. you cannot bribe them to ask for money to buy a local alliance and then deny them consent.

So yes, you can bribe them irrespective of who is the president: the rule is just saying that if you bribe the commander to buy the local alliance then: if Crown is president, they will give consent; and if you are president you MuST give consent.

Does this help?

Ricky

articles.body:
[q="MartinBG"]... because the crown president always gives consent. ...[/q]

NOTE: the consent the President gives is consent for the Commander to take money from the Treasury.

The PROMISE CUBES are the bribe to make the Commander seek to buy Local Alliances.

It doesn't matter who is President; if the Crown is Commander and BULL, they will not buy Local Alliances unless you bribe them with 2 Promise cubes.

[i]Once you have bribed them, it doesn't matter who is President, because a Crown president will always concede to a Crown Commander, and if you are the President then you MUST concede to the bribe (which is fine, because you are the one who did the bribe in the first place). 

This is significant in a 2-player game, because player A may bribe a Crown Commander to purchase a Local Alliance, but if player B is the president, they MAY, and CAN, choose not to concede to the request, and Player A would have wasted 2 promise cubes.
[/i]
